gpu.feature.name: Graphics cards
gpu.feature.desc: A graphics card line next to your CPUs: a division, research, a designer, production on the shared factory lines and a market of its own.

gpu.settings.rivals.tip: Named graphics card makers (NVIDIA, ATI, 3dfx and others) release cards of their own.
gpu.settings.synergy.tip: Share in one market helps the other: CPU rating up to +8%, graphics card rating up to +10%.
gpu.settings.news.tip: Mail about new leaders of the market segments. Mail about eras and about makers entering, leaving and merging always comes.
gpu.settings.consoleOrders.tip: Console makers offer long-term deliveries of graphics cards. Switched off, no new offers come; orders you accepted run on.
gpu.settings.cpuPriority.tip: Graphics cards take only the factory lines the CPUs leave free.

gpu.era.compute: The era of compute on graphics cards
gpu.mail.era.2d: Separate boards for the display have appeared on the market. For now they only need fast 2D graphics and a little video memory: research a 2D accelerator and DRAM, and the company has its first card.
gpu.mail.era.3d: The era of 3D accelerators has begun. The gaming segments are open: buyers expect cards with hardware 3D, and cards without it lose most of their rating. You need the 3D architecture, SGRAM memory and a fan on the heat sink.
gpu.mail.era.shader: The era of shaders has begun. Gaming cards without shader units lose rating in games, and they need noticeably more video memory. Research the shader architecture and GDDR3 memory.
gpu.mail.era.compute: The era of compute on graphics cards has begun. The compute segment is open: cards without compute units do not sell in it at all, and power draw affects what buyers choose. You need the general-purpose architecture and GDDR5 memory.
gpu.mail.era.ai: The era of AI accelerators has begun. The artificial intelligence segment is open: cards without tensor cores do not sell in it. You need the tensor architecture and HBM memory.
gpu.mail.era.rt: The era of ray tracing has begun. Gaming cards without hardware ray tracing lose rating. Research the ray tracing architecture and GDDR6 memory.

gpu.found.title: GPU division
gpu.found.intro: The graphics card division opens a second product line: its own laboratory, designer, production on the lines of your factory and its own market. Every node of the tree up to {0} is researched at once.
gpu.found.button.tip: Pays the founding cost, opens the nodes of the tree and the graphics card window.
gpu.found.confirm.title: Found the GPU division?
gpu.found.confirm.message: {0} will be spent and {1} nodes of the tree will open. The money is not refunded.
gpu.research.idle: The laboratory is idle. Pick a node in the tree below.
gpu.research.funding.tip: Share of the laboratory's full pace. More funding is faster research and a higher cost. The new value acts from the next day.
gpu.research.stop.tip: Stops the research in progress. Its progress is lost.
gpu.research.stop.title: Stop the research?
gpu.research.stop.message: Stop "{0}"? Its progress ({1}%) will be lost.
gpu.research.queueEmpty: The queue is empty: nodes you pick wait here while the laboratory is busy.
gpu.research.remove.tip: Takes the node out of the queue.
gpu.research.state.available: Click to start the research or put it in the queue.
gpu.design.arch.tip: Decides what the die can do: how many transistors a block takes, how many operations a block does per clock and which features it has (3D, shaders). New architectures are researched on the Research tab.
gpu.design.node.tip: A finer node puts more transistors on the same area and uses less power. The choice is from your company's nodes.
gpu.design.memory.tip: The type sets the data rate, the buses allowed and the largest size. Changing it changes the lists of buses and sizes.
gpu.design.bus.tip: Memory bandwidth = bus width / 8 × memory data rate. A narrow bus cannot feed the blocks: performance is held back by memory.
gpu.design.cooler.tip: The lower the thermal resistance, the cooler the die at the same power. A hot die fails more often.
gpu.design.die.tip: A larger area gives more transistors and blocks, but a dearer die, more failures and fewer dies per wafer. The limit is the largest die of the year.
gpu.design.clock.tip: Share of the highest clock of the architecture (the clock of your CPUs × the architecture's ratio). A higher clock means more performance, power, heat and failures.
gpu.design.vram.tip: Powers of two up to the limit of the memory type. With less memory than a segment asks for, the card's rating there drops (see the table below). Memory is most of the unit cost.
gpu.design.name: Name
gpu.design.missing: The designer is not available: no {0}. Research what is missing on the Research tab.
gpu.design.seg.col.name: Segment
gpu.design.started: Project "{0}" started: cost {1}, time {2}. Follow it on the Lineup tab.
gpu.design.stat.transistors.tip: Process node density × die area (with your density research).
gpu.design.stat.units.tip: Transistors / transistors per block of the architecture ({0}).
gpu.design.stat.maxClock.tip: The clock of your CPUs ({1}) × the architecture's ratio ({0}). The card does not run faster.
gpu.design.stat.bandwidth.tip: Bus ({0}-bit) / 8 × memory data rate ({1} MT/s). The bandwidth needed is compute power × bytes per operation. Have to need: {2}.
gpu.design.stat.perf.tip: Compute power × (bandwidth have / need)^{2} when memory falls short. The ratio is {0} now, the loss {1}.
gpu.design.stat.power.tip: Grows with die area and clock, falls with a finer node.
gpu.design.stat.temp.tip: Ambient ({0} °C) + power × the cooler's thermal resistance. Above {1} °C failures grow fast.
gpu.design.stat.failure.tip: Share of dies that fail: grows with temperature, the complexity of the architecture and the clock against the highest.
gpu.design.stat.dies.tip: Dies that fit a wafer ({0} mm) at the yield of the node ({1}), of all that would fit.
gpu.design.stat.unitCost.tip: The die (with failures and the price of the wafer) + video memory + board + cooler.
gpu.design.stat.projectCost.tip: The project of the architecture + a share of the node's project + the project of the memory type, with your company's development modifiers.
gpu.design.stat.projectDays.tip: Time of the architecture + time of the memory type.
gpu.lineup.mode.tip: The mode is changed on the graphics cards page of the Mods hub (the "CPU first" switch). GPU first: the cards take lines first, the CPUs get the rest.
gpu.lineup.project.pause.tip: Stops the progress and the spending on the project.
gpu.lineup.project.resume.tip: Carries on from where the project stopped.
gpu.lineup.project.cancel.tip: Deletes the project. The money spent is not refunded.
gpu.lineup.project.cancel.title: Cancel the project?
gpu.lineup.project.cancel.message: Cancel the development of "{0}"? The money spent is not refunded.
gpu.lineup.productionOff: Graphics card production is switched off by the self-check: no lines are reserved. The reason is on the graphics cards page of the Mods hub.

gpu.lineup.sell.tip: A card that is switched off leaves the market; its stock and lines stay.

gpu.lineup.unitsPerDay.tip: How many cards a day you order from the foundry. A number of your own switches Auto off.
gpu.lineup.auto.tip: The lines (or the order) follow the demand of the last seven days.
gpu.lineup.lastMonth: Last month: sold {0}, revenue {1}, costs {2}, profit {3}
gpu.lineup.release.tip: Opens the launch window: price, selling, lines.
gpu.lineup.retire.tip: The stock is sold at a reduced price, the lines are freed and the card goes to the archive.
gpu.lineup.retire.title: Retire the card?

gpu.release.sell.tip: Switch off to build a stock first: the card gets no buyers, its stock and lines are kept.

gpu.release.unitsPerDay.tip: How many cards a day you order from the foundry. You can change it later on the Lineup tab.
gpu.release.noLines: Your factory has no lines: assign them later on the Lineup tab.
gpu.release.noUnits: The order can be set on the Lineup tab.
gpu.release.button.tip: The card goes on the market at this price.
gpu.release.later.tip: The card stays ready to launch on the Lineup tab.

gpu.console.title: Console orders
gpu.console.title.tip: Console makers order graphics cards years ahead at a fixed price. An offer comes as a letter: you can accept it when you have a suitable card. Cards are shipped from the stock of the card before retail; missed deliveries cancel the order and lower your reputation.
gpu.console.offer.subject: {0}: console graphics chip order
gpu.console.offer.body: {0} asks for {1} cards a day at about {2} for {3}. Reply by {4}. The order is tied to your best card that is fast enough for the segment; cards are shipped from stock before retail. If more than {6} of the volume is missed over {5} days, the order is cancelled and your reputation drops by {7}.
gpu.console.accept.tip: The order is tied to your best suitable card. The price and the daily volume are fixed now.
gpu.console.decline.tip: The offer closes with no consequences.
